correctness.rationale: The lower positive-real-part bounds place L and M in the principal logarithm domains. Taylor expansion at zero gives the ordinary powers-of-two Dirichlet series for every Re s>0; α=0 is zero. For α≠0, chain differentiation gives H′=αM^(α−1)/((1−z)L). By periodicity and the simple zero of 1−2^(−s) at each boundary singularity, at local Euclidean distance ρ the measure density is comparable to α²σρ⁻² W(ρ), with W(ρ)=log(e/ρ)⁻²(log log(e/ρ))^(2α−2). A box abutting a singularity contains a fixed angular sector at radii comparable to h, giving the lower mass bound cα²hW(h). For boxes within 2h of a singularity, polar integration is bounded by Cα²∫₀^(4h)W(ρ)dρ, at most C′α²hW(h) since W is eventually increasing and W(4h) is comparable to W(h). Away from singularities but still in their neighborhoods, ρ⁻²W(ρ) is eventually decreasing in ρ, so at distance at least 2h the density bound integrated over a box is O(α²hW(h)). Uniformly regular boxes give O(h³). The resulting per-scale profile tends to zero below one, stays bounded and positive at one, and diverges above one. The unweighted mass per h is bounded at small scales for every fixed α; at larger scales each period has finite weighted derivative mass, with exponential decay at large σ, so μ(Q)/h stays bounded. This gives BMOA membership and verifies the LMOA hypotheses or their failure as appropriate. Tong–Wang–Yuan Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 then give all the operator assertions on both spaces, including the critical weak-compactness and complete-continuity exclusions.
residual_risks: The constants are for fixed α, not uniform in α. No essential-norm constant is established.
